ios.desc:
Vibe is a fast, minimal player for your music files.

Waveform view
Vibe draws every track as a full waveform. Drag it to scrub, swipe sideways to move between tracks.

Just plays your files
Play files on your iPhone, in iCloud Drive, or in Dropbox from the Files app or the built-in file picker.

No library to import
There is no database to rebuild and nothing to sync.

Vibe's own audio engine
MP3, AAC, MP4/M4A, MP2, AIFF, WAV, and FLAC, played through Vibe's own audio engine with high-quality sample-rate conversion.

Widgets
Small and medium widgets show the current track with its artwork and seekable waveform.

Free and open source
Vibe collects nothing and shows no ads. The full source is on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license.

quotes.text:
Vibe, my Winamp-like MacOS music player.

I use it every day, but had stopped dev on it a few years ago. Fable has gotten me excited to take it off the shelf and add a bunch of features I've been wanting for a while. Working on localization now.

https://github.com/cmicali/vibe

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/vibe-music-player/id1582482361
quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (August 2026)

quotes.text:
Hi All - I've been missing Winamp for a long time and  could not find a simple, fast audio player for macOS that I liked.

So, I built Vibe. It's a fast, minimal music file  player for Mac. It's written in Objective-C and optimized heavily for speed, resource use, and quality. ~12Mb app. No accounts, telemetry, or bloat.

It's free and open source: https://github.com/cmicali/vibe

Also available on the Mac App Store if you prefer: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/vibe-music-player/id1582482361?mt=12

I started this before "Vibe" had it's meaning changed, so it was completely hand-written for the first 4-5 years. Now I am using agents to speed up progress and implement things I otherwise wouldn't have had the time to do.

I would love any feedback, ideas, feature requests etc.
